item.title: Chaining Deep Link Injection with SQLi to Leak Sensitive Data from an iOS App
item.description:
This is my writeup for the Flipcoin Wallet iOS challenge by Mobile Hacking Labs - a two-part challenge involving deep link abuse and SQL injection that chains together really nicely.

Understanding the Challenge

The app is a crypto banking app with Flipcoin as its currency. Features:

  • Receive coins via QR code
  • Send coins to other accounts
  • Transaction history
  • Crypto news tab

The challenge description mentions SQLi and deeplink exploitation. The goal is to extract recovery keys of other users.

item.title: Defeating Multi-Layer Anti-Reversing Protections on iOS with Static Analysis and Frida
item.description:
This is my writeup for the Captain NoHook iOS challenge by Mobile Hacking Labs - combining multiple runtime checks, a non-exported debugger trap, and a hidden flag buried in memory.

Overview

A classic mobile RASP / anti-reversing puzzle. Goal: bypass the app’s reverse-engineering/compliance checks and find the hidden flag in memory.

Combined static analysis (radare2 / nm) with dynamic instrumentation (Frida) and Objection for memory inspection.

1. Static Discovery with r2 / nm

Loaded the app binary into r2 and searched for symbols/functions containing the term compliant. That quickly pointed at the high-level check deciding whether the device is “noncompliant”.
